title: MCP server family response envelope
description: The unified response envelope emitted by mediation.build_envelope, vendored byte-identically into cinii-mcp, jstage-mcp, ndl-mcp, korea-scholarship-mcp, semantic-scholar-mcp and openalex-mcp. Schema version 2.3.0. Every interpretation key is a typed field, never prose: the envelope reports what was searched and how the result set should be read, and never composes a summary or a relevance score. Diagnostic codes are a closed per-server registry documented in each README, so `code` is constrained here only as a string.

schema_version.description: Version of this envelope schema, not of the server package.

operation.description: The tool operation that produced the envelope, e.g. 'search_articles', 'get_record', 'resolve_doi', 'list_issues'. Operations whose name begins 'search' chose a term; the rest were handed an identifier.

searched_for.description: Headline: the term actually sent to the database, hoisted to the top of the envelope so it is not lost when an assistant relays results. Present on search operations only; fetch operations omit it because no term was chosen.

term.description: The normalised query string as sent, not as typed.

matching.description: Same value as the envelope's matching_mode; repeated here so the headline stands alone.

input_terms.description: What the caller supplied, before normalisation.

normalized.description: What was actually sent to the API. This, with `script`, is the record of any rendering the assistant performed between the caller's language and the corpus.

params.description: Request parameters as issued, with credential-bearing keys stripped by the caller before the envelope is built.

matching_mode.description: How the source matched the query, e.g. 'metadata_conjunction' (CiNii), 'full_text_broad' (J-STAGE), 'harvest_window_filter' (OAI windows). It tells the reader how to interpret result.total and result.breadth.

total.description: Whatever the source reported. Where a source reports no total, the caller passes the size of the window actually yielded and raises a truncation diagnostic, so a returned count is never mistaken for a corpus count.

breadth.description: Graduated set-size signal: none (0), narrow (1-50), broad (51-1000), very_broad (>1000). Thresholds are deliberately low so a few hundred hits that look like a literature are marked rather than passed through clean.

items.description: May be empty. An empty array with a zero-result diagnostic is a successful nil search, not an error.

coverage_note.description: Free-text statement of what the corpus does and does not cover, where the source's coverage would otherwise be read as the field's.

attribution.description: The credit line the data provider's terms require, carried in every response.

suggestions.description: Optional. Alternative queries offered to the caller; present only when the server has one to make.

script.description: Dominant script of the normalised query. Digits, whitespace and punctuation are ignored; an empty string reports 'latin' as the n/a case. A 'latin' value against a Japanese or Korean corpus is the romanisation trap and raises SCRIPT_LATIN_QUERY.

code.description: A member of the server's closed diagnostic registry, documented in its README.

receipt.description: Loggable and citable: a stable hash over the normalised query and its parameters, plus the identifiers returned. The hash verifies a term already held; it cannot be inverted to produce one, so a deposit of receipts alone deposits nothing re-runnable. The unit of deposit is the envelope.

issued_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, seconds precision, local offset.

query_hash.description: SHA-256 over a deterministic JSON serialisation of {q: normalized, params}.

result_ids.description: First available identifier per item, in order: doi, kci_id, crid, naid, oai_id. Items carrying none are omitted, so this array may be shorter than items.

romanized.description: Null unless the source supplies a romanisation. The servers do not generate one: a machine-transliterated string presented as bibliographic data is a fabrication with the shape of a fact.

authors.description: Author objects are passed through by make_item, so their shape is set by the caller and is deliberately open. Two shapes are in use in the family: the Japanese servers emit {ja, en}; korea-scholarship-mcp emits {name, name_en, affiliation, orcid}. The properties below are typed where they appear; a server may add its own.

matched_in.description: Which field the match was made in, or 'unknown' where the source does not say.

extra.description: Source-specific fields that have no place in the shared shape.
